name: Capture and confirm trades (one trade allocation)
summary: Every trade the internal desk executes is split into allocations across pools and client accounts, and each allocation must agree with the broker's confirmation before its settlement instruction goes to the custodian. Most equity, bond and FX allocations match automatically in the matching service within hours; trade support analysts work the exceptions, asking the trader to confirm terms or the broker to correct its details, forcing small commission differences within tolerance and chasing missing confirmations before the noon T+1 matching deadline. Derivatives are confirmed against ISDA terms, some on paper, and passed to collateral management. Broker instruction errors, manual allocations, paper derivative confirmations and volume peaks on rebalancing days cause most of the work.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about $40 billion of internally traded public assets, a four-person trading desk and a six-person trade support team using a software-as-a-service order management system and a central matching service.
baseline.notes: T+2 settlement in Canada and the US from September 2017; trades of external managers are processed by those managers and the custodian and are not in this process.

trigger: A trader completes an executed order in the order management system and its allocations are sent for matching, or a broker's confirmation arrives for an allocation.
end_state: The allocation is matched and affirmed and its settlement instruction is released to the custodian, or the derivative is confirmed and passed to collateral management.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at month and quarter ends with pool rebalancing, client flows and overlay adjustments; very high on pool launch and transition days.

evidence.note: Organisation file's demand driver: orders split into allocations across pools and client accounts plus FX and derivative trades.
Cost from the organisation file (Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto basis). FTE author estimate from hands-on time and volume; the same analysts also manage settlement fails.
Cost from the organisation file (Job Bank NOC 10010 basis).

steps.name: Complete the executed ticket and confirm the allocation
steps.description: After execution the trader checks that the fills from the trading platform carry the right broker, price, commission and fees, and confirms the split of the block across pools and client accounts set before the trade; most splits are calculated by the order management system pro rata.

error.defect_description: Wrong account, quantity split, price or broker on an allocation.

evidence.note: Block orders are allocated to client accounts by management-set methods and allocations are approved (SOC 1 baseline objective). Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Enrich the allocation with settlement instructions and send it to matching
steps.description: The book of record adds the broker's standing settlement instructions and the custodian account, calculates the settlement date and net amount, and sends the allocation to the matching service and the trade to post-trade compliance; derivatives go to the derivative confirmation route.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

next.condition: standing settlement instruction missing or out of date

evidence.note: Matching covers trade details and settlement instructions among trade-matching parties. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Broker sends its confirmation to the matching service
steps.description: The broker or FX bank books the allocations in its own system and sends its confirmation to the matching service; trades done in Asian or European hours or late in the day arrive the next morning.

error.defect_description: The broker's confirmation differs from the model manager's allocation.

evidence.note: Central matching between investment managers and brokers; timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Matching service compares the trade details
steps.description: The matching service compares security, quantity, price, commission, fees, net amount, trade and settlement dates and settlement instructions within agreed tolerances and flags matched, mismatched or unconfirmed allocations.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: National Instrument 24-101: dealer and adviser policies must achieve matching of institutional DAP/RAP trades no later than noon Eastern Time on T+1, with quarterly exception reports if under 90 per cent; the model manager provides a trade-matching statement

evidence.note: Deadline and threshold from NI 24-101; about 92% same-day matching for automated users (2025 data, used as an order of magnitude).

steps.name: Investigate the unmatched allocation
steps.description: A trade support analyst opens the exception queue, compares the model manager's allocation with the broker's confirmation field by field and finds the cause, usually commission or fee rounding, a quantity split, a wrong settlement instruction or settlement date, or occasionally a real trade error.

error.defect_description: The analyst blames the wrong side and the exception repeats.

next.condition: The model manager's terms may be wrong
trade error: wrong security, size or side

evidence.note: Manual allocation and instruction handling create errors and fails. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Chase the broker for a missing confirmation
steps.description: The analyst emails or calls the broker's middle office for confirmations still missing late in the day or on the morning of T+1, and watches the noon T+1 deadline.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

next.condition: still unmatched near noon on T+1

evidence.note: Matching deadline of noon on T+1 for all trades since the 2017 move to T+2. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Trader confirms the correct trade terms
steps.description: The analyst asks the trader which price, commission or allocation is right; the trader checks the execution record and confirms whether the model manager's ticket or the broker's confirmation is wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Operations may not change trade economics without front-office confirmation (SOC 1 objective that trades are properly authorized and recorded)

next.condition: The model manager's ticket is wrong

evidence.note: Trades properly authorized and recorded. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Ask the broker to correct and resend its confirmation
steps.description: The analyst sends the broker the correct details and asks it to cancel and resend its confirmation, then waits for it to match.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Approve a manual match within tolerance
steps.description: For a small commission or fee difference within the agreed tolerance, the manager reviews the difference and approves forcing the match so the trade can settle, recording the reason.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Trade support procedures: tolerance for commission and fee differences and manager approval of forced matches

evidence.note: Common tolerance practice. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Amend or cancel and rebook the allocation
steps.description: The analyst amends the allocation in the order management system, or cancels and rebooks it, with the trader's confirmation attached, and the corrected allocation is resent to the matching service.

error.defect_description: The rebooked allocation carries a new keying error.

evidence.note: Common practice. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Affirm the match and release the settlement instruction to the custodian
steps.description: Once matched, the affirmation is recorded and the settlement instruction goes to the custodian over SWIFT, and the settled-trade status will feed reconciliations and cash management.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: SOC 1 baseline control objective: trades properly authorized, allocated, settled and recorded accurately, completely and timely

evidence.note: SOC 1 trading and settlement objectives; the model manager's SOC 1 Type I report in 2021.

steps.name: Check the derivative trade and send it for confirmation
steps.description: For an OTC forward or swap the analyst checks the ticket against the counterparty's ISDA and credit support terms and affirms it on the electronic confirmation platform or waits for the dealer's paper confirmation; for futures the analyst checks the clearing broker's give-up.

error.defect_description: A term such as the reset date or day count is keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Interest rate derivatives were mostly confirmed electronically, equity derivatives less so. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Dealer or clearing broker returns its confirmation
steps.description: The dealer affirms on the platform or sends a paper or PDF confirmation; the clearing broker confirms the futures give-up. Paper confirmations for less standard trades take days.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Outstanding confirmations averaged 1.0 business day for rates and 6.1 for equity derivatives (2013).

steps.name: Compare the derivative confirmation with the ticket
steps.description: The analyst compares every economic and legal term of the dealer's confirmation with the ticket and the ISDA terms, and routes differences to the exception process.

error.defect_description: A legal term difference is missed.

evidence.note: Common practice. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Sign the paper confirmation as authorised signatory
steps.description: The manager reviews the analyst's comparison of the paper confirmation, signs it under the model manager's signing authorities for ISDA trades and returns it to the dealer by email or courier.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Signing authority policy for derivative confirmations under ISDA master agreements

evidence.note: Common practice. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Pass the confirmed derivative to collateral management
steps.description: The analyst records the confirmed derivative so the collateral team includes it in margin and exposure calculations and the counterparty exposure review, and files the confirmation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: OTC positions are consolidated by counterparty with collateral captured and exposures monitored daily. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Manager escalates an aged unmatched trade
steps.description: The manager calls the broker's operations lead, or involves the trader or head of trading, to resolve trades still unmatched near noon on T+1 that risk failing, and logs the item.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Later matching leaves too little time to avoid failed trades. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Head of trading decides how to correct a trade error
steps.description: When the wrong security, size or side was traded or allocated, the head of trading decides how to correct it, who bears the cost and whether a client is affected, with compliance informed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Trade errors and guideline breaches are a SOC 1 baseline area. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Log the trade error and its cost
steps.description: The manager records the error, its cause, cost and correction in the trade error register for compliance and the quarterly review, and instructs the analyst to cancel and rebook the allocation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Trade error policy and SOC 1 control objective over trade errors: errors recorded, corrected and clients made whole

evidence.note: SOC 1 baseline area. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Set up or correct the broker's standing settlement instruction
steps.description: The analyst obtains the broker's new standing settlement instructions through an authenticated message or verifies them by calling a known contact, enters them, and a second person approves before the allocation is enriched again.

error.defect_description: An instruction is keyed with a wrong account.

control.basis: Payment and settlement instruction changes verified through a known contact and approved by a second person

evidence.note: Verify banking changes with a known number and have two people approve changes to standing instructions. Per-allocation times and exception shares are author estimates; no published time study was found.

exceptions.name: Mismatch with the broker
exceptions.description: Commission, price, quantity split, settlement date or instruction differs and is fixed by the model manager, the broker or a forced match.

exceptions.name: Missing broker confirmation
exceptions.description: The broker has not confirmed by end of day; the analyst chases and the manager escalates near the noon T+1 deadline.

exceptions.name: Derivative confirmation
exceptions.description: Futures and OTC derivatives are confirmed against ISDA terms, some on paper signed by the manager, and passed to collateral management.

exceptions.name: Trade error
exceptions.description: The wrong security, size or side was traded or allocated; the head of trading decides the correction and the error is logged.

exceptions.name: Missing or outdated settlement instruction
exceptions.description: The broker's standing settlement instruction is missing or changed and must be verified and approved before matching.

pain_points.description: Brokers' wrong or outdated settlement instructions and commission rounding cause most mismatches, which are worked one by one in an exception queue.
The noon T+1 matching deadline under T+2 settlement leaves little time to fix late or missing confirmations before trades fail.
Less standard derivatives are still confirmed on paper and take days, needing manual comparison and a signature.
Allocation volumes spike on month ends, rebalancing and pool transition days, when exception queues grow.

evidence.note: Author estimate from the organisation file's description of rebalancing and pool flows.

sources.title: Shortening the Settlement Cycle: Final CSA Amendments to NI 24-101
sources.supports: Canada moved to T+2 settlement on 5 September 2017; the institutional trade matching deadline became noon on T+1 for all trades because later matching leaves too little time to avoid fails. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: Same-day matching rates a crucial indicator in run-up to T+1 in Europe
sources.supports: Users of automated trade matching achieve an average 92.4% same-day matching (equities 94.83%, fixed income 89.9%, some markets as low as 78.5%); firms using fax, email or spreadsheets for allocation have higher error and fail rates (2025, outside the reference period).

sources.title: ISDA Publishes 2013 Operations Benchmarking Survey
sources.supports: 77 firms: 100% of eligible credit derivatives and 92% of interest rate derivatives confirmed electronically; outstanding confirmations 0.3 business days for credit, 1.0 for rates and 6.1 for equity derivatives (before the reference period).

assumptions: One case is one allocation of an executed internal trade to one pool or client account. External managers' trades are matched by those managers and the custodian and are outside this process.
The process ends when the settlement instruction is released; settlement monitoring and fails belong to trade-settlement-fails, which lists this process as its main trigger.

About 90% of equity, bond and FX allocations match automatically on first pass; the 2025 European matching rate is used only as an order of magnitude because no Canadian figure for the period was found.

The model manager is exempt from adviser registration under the 2017 OSC decisions, so the NI 24-101 obligations fall on its dealers and custodian; the model manager's part is the trade-matching statement and timely matching.
The head of trading takes part for trade errors although the process map lists only the trader, trade support analyst and manager; the role exists in the organisation file.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file: Job Bank Toronto wages deflated 9% to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading.

Staffing: about 1.2 FTE stated (0.95 analyst); hands-on time times volume implies a similar figure. With 1.75 analyst FTE already on settlements and reconciliations, the six-person team has room for counterparty onboarding and corporate action support.
Per-allocation times, exception shares and waits are author estimates (tier C).
